latest_release.name: AIVPN 1.2.0
latest_release.body:
**Dual-stack networking, signed distribution and application hardening.** 1.2.0 extends IPv6 across the tunnel, adds large management messages and new bootstrap and mask distribution channels, and fixes session, storage and platform security issues. Inter-server connections now use masked handshake sessions throughout.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Breaking release.** The initial exchange moves to InitialV2 and is incompatible with 1.1.0 and earlier 1.2.0 development builds. There is no automatic fallback. Update servers, pool/site/chain nodes and every client, including embedded mobile cores, together.

## Highlights

- **IPv6 across the tunnel**: the server assigns an IPv6 address, prefix and MTU through `ServerHello`; desktop and mobile clients apply it, with source validation, client isolation and QoS for both address families.
- **InitialV2 handshake**: separate KDF v2 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a random 24-byte nonce; data and management commands require confirmed PFS.
- **QUIC and RTC masks**: bidirectional QUIC v1/TLS 1.3 with HTTP/3 CONNECT-UDP; Zoom, Telemost, SberJazz, Telegram calls and WhatsApp masks over ICE/DTLS/SRTP and TURN.
- **Adaptive data pacing**: queues adapt to persistent delay instead of stalling the tunnel at a fixed packet rate; `upload_shaping` / `downlink_shaping` select `adaptive`, `full` or `off`.
- **Signed distribution**: release artifacts and mask archives are signed with Ed25519; passive mask delivery over DNS TXT, PNG, Bitcoin OP_RETURN and Ethereum calldata, and email bootstrap through JMAP.
- **Platform clients**: Android Material 3 interface and automatic network recovery, Linux Material/Breeze and Windows Fluent layouts, persistent Windows kill switch.
- **Security**: site peers no longer receive pool database or management rights, live revocation of inter-server nodes, enforced signatures in `production-secure`, and dependency fixes including RUSTSEC-2026-0381, -0382, -0385 and -0387.

## Upgrade notes

1. Update all servers, pool/site/chain nodes and clients together.
2. Remove an explicit `pool.transport=legacy`; an omitted value now selects `masked`.
3. Configure the client database: server operation without one is removed.
4. Rotate previously used static keys and distribute trusted release and operator public keys before enabling signature enforcement.
5. Replace an explicit `telegram_mtproto_v1` mask selection with `telegram_calls_v1`.

Settings and verification steps: [docs/RELEASE_1.2.0.md](https://github.com/infosave2007/aivpn/blob/v1.2.0/docs/RELEASE_1.2.0.md).

## Verifying downloads

Every asset ships with a detached Ed25519 signature (`.sig`). Server binaries also ship with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

```bash
sha256sum -c aivpn-server-linux-x86_64.SHA256SUMS
```

## Contributors

Thanks to @vaminakov for the 1.2.0 work (#82).

**Full changelog**: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/infosave2007/aivpn/blob/v1.2.0/CHANGELOG.md#120---2026-10-27) · [v1.1.0...v1.2.0](https://github.com/infosave2007/aivpn/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0)
